subject: Post-incident RCA & Recovery Commitments — Cascade Commerce SLA Readout
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@cascadecommerce.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reed <tom.reed@cascadecommerce.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Severe latency & errors impacting checkout — urgent

Jasmine / Redwood team,

We experienced a major degradation on our production inference path this morning between 08:45-09:30 PDT. Symptoms: 10x request latency, 20% 5xx error rate, and multiple timeouts surfaced across storefront checkout and recommendation endpoints. Our site health dashboard shows a sustained throughput drop while retry traffic spiked.

We pulled logs and attached a support bundle (cascade_support_bundle_20270620.zip). Can you provide: 1) an initial RCA hypothesis, 2) immediate mitigations you're applying, and 3) when we can expect a formal RCA and remediation timeline?

This incident is impacting us across EU and US buyers and we need an executive readout for our CTO by EOD tomorrow. Please treat as high priority.

Thanks,
Elena Soto
Sr. Ops Manager, Cascade Commerce
Elena.soto@cascadecommerce.com
[Attachment: cascade_support_bundle_20270620.zip (log bundle)]

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@cascadecommerce.com>
Cc: Tom Reed <tom.reed@cascadecommerce.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-20T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Severe latency & errors impacting checkout — urgent

Hi Elena — thank you for the heads up and the bundle. We're investigating with priority. Initial notes from our on-call: several GPU workers experienced abnormal memory pressure leading to frequent host-side OOMs and degraded throughput; that in turn caused cascading retries which saturated the remaining workers and increased latency.

Immediate actions we've taken (already applied):
- Disabled prefetching on the affected model pool to reduce KV cache churn (temporary).
- Increased autoscale headroom for Cascade's dedicated pool by +25% to absorb retry bursts.
- Enabled a fallback model variant with smaller context length for time-sensitive endpoints to reduce per-token compute.

We are preparing an interim RCA and a follow-up readout. Proposed exec readout: 2027-06-21 10:00 PDT (30 min); please confirm availability. Interim RCA attached: rca_draft_v1.pdf.

I'll circulate a formal action tracker with owners and deadlines once we complete root-cause verification.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll prioritize stabilization and a clear remediation plan.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.ai
[Attachment: rca_draft_v1.pdf (interim RCA)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Soto <elena.soto@cascadecommerce.com>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@cascadecommerce.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Technical findings — memory-pressure + retry amplification (INF-9812)

Team / Cascade,

Quick technical summary (working hypothesis):
- Root cause: A change in model prefetch scheduling combined with a longer average sequence length in the morning traffic window resulted in increased KV cache eviction rates on the dedicated pool nodes. Evictions increased host memory allocation for rebuilds and pushed several processes into host-side swapping → intermittent OOM restarts.
- Amplifier: Client-side retries (short retry backoff) plus our autoscaler reacting to perceived unhealthy workers caused a cascade where new workers were overloaded with warmups and large context requests.

Evidence pulled: stack traces and GPU metrics in the attached bundle show repeated CUDA driver warnings at 08:42:30 and host OOMs at 08:44:12. Repro steps inside INF-9812.

Immediate/near-term mitigations we implemented:
1) Rolling restart of the seven affected worker pods with conservative concurrency (completed 09:05).
2) Temporarily disabled model prefetching flag for Cascade pool (config: prefetch=false).
3) Scoped request rate-limit at the gateway for heavy-context routes to reduce peak tail latency.

Next steps (tracked in Jira INF-9812):
- Short-term (48–72 hrs): increase eviction buffer and tune cache retention policy; add stricter retry backoff guidance on client SDKs. Owner: Karthik Iyer; ETA: 2027-06-23.
- Medium-term (2–4 weeks): implement adaptive prefetching tied to per-model context distribution and improve autoscaler hysteresis. Owner: Markus Klein; ETA: 2027-07-15.
- Long-term (quarter): QA and load test with realistic sequence-length distributions and expand runbook for fallback variants. Owner: Grace O'Connor; ETA: 2027-08-15.

I will update INF-9812 with logs and a reproducible test harness.

Date: 2027-06-23T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: RCA delivered & action tracker — next steps and commitments

Elena / Tom — thanks again for your time on Thursday. Attached is the finalized RCA and the action-tracker spreadsheet capturing owners, Jira links, deadlines, and acceptance criteria. Below is the executive summary and commitments we discussed.

Executive summary:
- Incident: Production degradation 2027-06-20 08:45-09:30 PDT; peak 5xx rate 20% and 10x median latency for heavy-context endpoints.
- Root cause: KV cache eviction amplification due to prefetch scheduling interacting with a shift in traffic sequence lengths; host memory pressure caused worker restarts which amplified retries and saturated capacity.
- Impact surface: Checkout and recommendations across US/EU regions on dedicated pool for Cascade Commerce.

Formal commitments & owners (from tracker):
- INF-9812: Increase KV cache buffer and harden eviction policy — Owner: Karthik Iyer; Due: 2027-06-23 (in progress).
- INF-9874: Implement client SDK retry-backoff guidance and server-side soft-throttles for heavy-context routes — Owner: Grace O'Connor; Due: 2027-06-30.
- INF-9921: Adaptive prefetching prototype and autoscaler hysteresis tuning — Owner: Markus Klein; Due: 2027-07-15.
- Incident follow-up runbook and load-testing scenario added to QA pipeline — Owner: Jasmine Liu; Due: 2027-07-07.

Billing & credits: I've looped our billing operations team; they will review the incident window and SLA terms for potential crediting. Contact: billing@redwood.ai (note: we'll provide a policy summary and a proposed credit within 5 business days).

Attachments included: rca_final_20270623.pdf, cascade_action_tracker_20270623.xlsx.

We'll keep the Jira tickets updated and will schedule a 1:1 with your engineering leads if you'd like deeper technical walkthroughs. Please reply if you want an expanded remediation timeline or to shift any due dates.

Regards,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
